title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 105: Saffron: The Golden Threads of History
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 105 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Saffron: The Golden Threads of History

Paragraph 1. Saffron is the most expensive cooking spice in the world. It has a sweet smell, a bright golden color, and a light bitter taste. People get saffron from the dry red threads, called stigmas, inside a purple flower. Farmers have grown this special plant for more than four thousand years in lands near the Mediterranean Sea and Western Asia. Long ago, people did not only use saffron in food. They also used it to color cloth, make sweet smoke in temples, and treat eye or breathing sicknesses.

Paragraph 2. Unlike wild plants, the saffron plant cannot grow from seeds. Because of this, it cannot live alone in nature without help from humans. To grow new plants, farmers must dig up the round parts under the ground, called corms. They break off the small baby parts and put them back into dry soil by hand. If farmers stop doing this hard work, the saffron plant will completely disappear from the Earth in a few years.

Paragraph 3. Saffron costs so much money because picking it takes huge human work. The purple flowers only open for two or three weeks in late autumn. Workers must pick every flower by hand early in the morning. Strong sun at noon can hurt the fragile color and smell inside the flower. Machines cannot help because they break the soft plant parts. Workers need about 150,000 flowers and forty hours of hard work to make just one kilogram of dry saffron.

Paragraph 4. After picking, workers carefully dry the fresh red threads over warm fires or in heated rooms. Fresh threads have almost no smell, so drying gives saffron its famous scent. However, too much heat burns the threads and weakens their health value. Because pure saffron is worth as much as silver, some dishonest sellers mix it with cheap things like yellow flower petals or oil to make it heavier. Today, science labs test saffron to keep it pure.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "They also used it to color cloth..." (color = colour).
Đoạn 2: "...dig up the round parts under the ground, called corms."
Đoạn 3: "Strong sun at noon can hurt the fragile color..." (hurt = damage).
Đoạn 4: "...mix it with cheap things like yellow flower petals or oil to make it heavier."

q5.text: Saffron is cheaper than most other spices used in cooking today.

steps: Đoạn 1: "Saffron is the most expensive cooking spice in the world." → Đắt nhất thế giới, trái ngược với cheaper.

q6.text: The saffron plant cannot survive naturally in the wild without human help.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...it cannot live alone in nature without help from humans."

q7.text: Modern farming machines are used to pick saffron flowers quickly at noon.

steps: Đoạn 3: Hoa được hái bằng tay từ sáng sớm (by hand early in the morning) và máy móc không dùng được (Machines cannot help).

q8.text: Most saffron sold today is grown by farmers in Western Asia.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bài chỉ nói cây được trồng ở Địa Trung Hải và Tây Á, không nhắc nơi nào sản xuất nhiều nhất hiện nay.
